customer_acme: hey team :wave: we've seen a sudden p50 jump on text-generation from ~120ms -> ~420ms starting ~48h ago. throughput (rps) from our side hasn't changed much. model: gpt-small-1 (hosted, us-west-2). sample request ids we captured: req_34a9c1, req_34a9c2, req_34b0d4. average tokens/client ~120, spikes to ~600 on some prompts. Can you help triage?

maya (Support): thanks — can you confirm which API route you're calling (/v1/generate vs /v1/chat) and paste 3 full request ids (the request id printed in the X-Request-Id header) and the exact prompt examples? If you can provide a curl reproduction that'd speed things up. Also, are you on Hosted or Dedicated capacity?

customer_acme: we're using /v1/chat. Hosted tier. three full ids: req_34a9c1-usw2-01, req_34a9c2-usw2-01, req_34b0d4-usw2-02. here's a trimmed prompt set (the actual payloads are similar):

"Hello, summarize: {{article_text}}"
"Write a short reply in <50 tokens about product pricing."

many of the slow ones are the summarize flow where article_text ~ 400-1,200 tokens.

samir (SRE): can you run the debug bundle collector script so we can get traces + server-side logs for those request ids? run this from a machine that can reach your API key: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/debug/bundles \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"request_ids": ["req_34a9c1-usw2-01", "req_34a9c2-usw2-01", "req_34b0d4-usw2-02"], "include_traces": true, "include_metrics": true}'

# response will be {"bundle_id":"bundle_1749123710","upload_url":"..."} then: 
# curl -s -X PUT <upload_url> --data-binary @debug-bundle.tar.gz
```

maya (Support): also please generate a small repro load profile: a CSV with two columns: timestamp_iso, concurrent_clients (or a short JSON list). We need to know your client concurrency and QPS when you observed the p50 jump. Example CSV header: `ts,clients` then lines like `2026-03-12T12:00:00Z,20`.

customer_acme: we can export our Grafana to CSV. At the time of the spike our gateway shows a steady ~80 concurrent clients and ~200 rps. I'll attach.

eli (ML Eng): to speed local reproduction we need: 1) exact prompt templates (with token counts), 2) a small promptset (10-30 prompts representative), 3) a scripted repro that issues requests at the same concurrency/QPS and token lengths. Suggested minimal repro (uses hey for concurrency):

```bash
# simple single-endpoint repro hitting chat generate endpoint (adjust headers/body)
CONCURRENCY=40
DURATION=60
cat prompts.jsonl | \
  xargs -I{} -P $CONCURRENCY curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{}'

# or using hey: hey -c 40 -q 3 -z 60s -m POST -D headers.txt -T application/json -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.inference/v1/chat
```

maya (Support): please also include the client-side timing breakdown (DNS, connect, TLS, time_to_first_byte, total_time) from any curl -w output you can capture. That helps distinguish network vs server token generation latency. Example: `curl -w "%{time_total} %{time_starttransfer} %{http_code}" -o /dev/null -s ...`

customer_acme: ok uploading the bundle now, and I'll attach prompts.jsonl + concurrency.csv + a small payload.sh that runs the hey/curled repro. ETA ~20m.

debug-bundle-bot: debug bundle upload received: bundle_1749123710 (size: 4.8MB) — processing.

samir (SRE): once the bundle is processed can you also share a short sample of slow response headers (the full X-Request-Id and X-Server-Latency) and the client curl -D response headers? If you see `x-server-latency: 350ms` but time_total is 420ms we know network contributed ~70ms.

eli (ML Eng): when you upload prompts.jsonl include token_count for each example. If possible, include two versions: one with warm cache (repeat prefix) and one cold. We'll try to reproduce cache warm/cold differences. Also note whether you pin a model version or use latest.

maya (Support): thanks — once we have bundle + repro script we'll assemble a reproducible pack and run it on Dedicated test cluster to compare p50/p95 with your traces. We'll keep you updated in this thread. :eyes:

customer_acme: awesome, thanks all. uploading now and will ping when done.
